what_it_does: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) is a technique that lets a computer do calculations on data that is still encrypted — the data never needs to be decrypted, so it stays private even on an untrusted server. One widely used FHE scheme is called TFHE, but it is extremely compute-intensive. Running TFHE on processing-in-memory (PIM) chips — chips that do math inside the memory module itself rather than shipping data back and forth to a distant processor — seems promising, but naive approaches create too much communication between different memory banks because unrelated data ends up stored far apart. This paper rearranges the order in which TFHE's sub-operations run so that data that needs to be used together is stored in the same memory bank, dramatically cutting the cross-bank traffic that would otherwise dominate runtime.
